clue.text: Evil confronted Anglicans in the intervening period

parts.note: evil or wrongdoing is sin
CE is the Church of England, the body of Anglicans

explanation.surface: Wickedness faced the Church of England during some interim.
explanation.definitionFit: Since as an adverb means from that time until now, covering the period in between.

clue.text: Promise to pay an underwriter

explanation.surface: An insurer undertakes to cover a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge regular payment is to subscribe, and a subscriber underwrites a loan or issue, splitting into under plus scribe.

clue.text: Unusual thing to observe in a club

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of thing are put in an odd order

parts.note: to spot is to notice or observe

explanation.surface: A curious sight is seen at a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns THING into NIGHT; the club is a place for evening entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue for late-night drinking and dancing.

clue.text: Relax in a Swansea seafood restaurant

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found within the words Swansea seafood

explanation.surface: Unwind at a fish restaurant in the Welsh city of Swansea.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to loosen or relax.

clue.text: Romantic offering means nothing to Mr Baker

parts.note: love is zero, nothing, in tennis scoring
Ken is the first name of Kenneth Baker, the British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A romantic gift means nothing at all to a man named Baker.
explanation.walkthrough: Kenneth Baker was a prominent British cabinet minister of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake given as a sign of affection is a romantic gift.

clue.text: Scrooge can appear in less well-known novel

indicators.note: appearing in means the first pieces sit inside the word for less

parts.note: taken as written
Scrooge, from Dickens, is the archetypal miser
can means is able

explanation.surface: A mean character may turn up in a lesser-known book.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo's Les Misérables is one of the most famous novels.

clue.text: Convey a little spirit and energy

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Communicate a touch of spirit and vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or transport.

clue.text: Boots which generate excitement

explanation.surface: Footwear that creates a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicks are slang for shoes or trainers, and getting your kicks is finding thrills.

clue.text: She tends to give directions to railway workers

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain
S and E are south and east, compass directions

explanation.surface: A woman habitually guides those working on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She tends to' reads as a habit; the definition is a carer who tends the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer looks after the sick, tending them.

clue.text: Sham American goes to Slough

parts.note: a slough is a swamp or bog
US stands for American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: A fake American heads off to the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town west of London, but here it is a common noun meaning swampy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, a sham or counterfeit.

clue.text: Racer is to show off an injury

parts.note: to sport something is to wear it proudly, to show it off
a scar is the mark of an injury

explanation.surface: Someone means to flaunt a wound they have suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast two-seater car built for speed is a kind of racer.

clue.text: Why one pursues a hobby when dividends are spent

explanation.surface: A pastime is followed while share income is used up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is followed for curiosity's sake, and once dividend income is spent there is no interest left.

clue.text: Make a reference to sound vision

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for vision is to be said out loud

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: Someone mentions sound vision, as an optician might.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote or mention a source is to refer to it.

clue.text: Fund established for young Catherine

explanation.surface: A charitable fund is set up in a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund of money is a kitty, and Kitty is a pet form of the name Catherine.

clue.text: Where one expect leis to be distributed

definitions.text: Where one expect leis to be distributed

indicators.note: being distributed means the letters of leis are dealt out into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Garlands of flowers are handed out on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: Leis are Hawaiian flower garlands, given to visitors on arrival, so an island is where one expects them to be handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in the Pacific is where garlands are traditionally handed out.

clue.text: Employers from the States about to return on Sunday

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: returning means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: American bosses are about to come back on a weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employers' here means those who use something, not bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who employ something are people who make use of it.

clue.text: Belief for which a Red Indian died

parts.note: the Cree are a Native North American people
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A faith for which a Native American lost his life.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs.

clue.text: Clocked on when under pressure to get the job done

definitions.text: under pressure to get the job done

explanation.surface: A worker is short of hours and in a hurry to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the clock hands forward is moving on the hour, and being hurried by a deadline is the idiom's everyday sense.

clue.text: Generally where the conquistadors made their fortune

definitions.text: where the conquistadors made their fortune

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, the Spanish adventurers grew rich at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Main was the Caribbean coast of the Americas plundered by Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: On the whole means mostly, and the conquistadors grew rich along the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Sympathetic partner resolved to include junior officer

indicators.note: including means the officer's letters go inside the reworked partner
resolved means the letters of partner are worked out into a new order

parts.note: PO is a pilot officer, a junior RAF rank

explanation.surface: A colleague decides to bring in a lowly officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in harmony and close accord with someone is being sympathetic.

clue.text: Ten nattier men arranged to put on a show

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these three words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten rather smart men are organised to stage a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance put on for an audience is a form of amusement.

clue.text: Small animal shelter in the Channel Islands

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Noah's ark sheltered the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A little refuge for creatures is found on a British island group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off Normandy; Sark is one of them, so the place is defined by where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small island belonging to that group off the French coast.

clue.text: Refuse to come to blows

explanation.surface: Someone declines to start a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap is rubbish or waste, and to scrap is to fight.

clue.text: Considers one option in local taxation

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a choice for council taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British property-based local tax before the council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge or consider it, and British councils levied rates on property.

clue.text: Where London prisoners were held fast

explanation.surface: Prisoners in London were kept firmly secured.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet Prison was a notorious London jail, and fleet as an adjective means swift.

clue.text: Cry you and I record

parts.note: you and I together make we
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Two people make a recording together.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is to cry.

clue.text: Bill has a yen to produce magazine article

parts.note: the Old Bill is British slang for the police, so a bill is a policeman
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A man named Bill longs to write a feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name; it is a police officer, from the Old Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy is journalistic text written for publication.

clue.text: Leans over the rotisserie

indicators.note: over means the word for leans is turned back to front

parts.note: something that tips leans or tilts

explanation.surface: Someone bends over a roasting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating skewer for roasting meat is a spit.

clue.text: Turned up in a demure trousseau

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of demure trousseau

explanation.surface: Something was found in a modest bride's wedding linen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'turned up' as found, but it describes a nose tilted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A retroussé nose is one tilted at the tip, French for tucked up.

clue.text: French dish given to old Greek writer

parts.note: plat is French for a dish or course

explanation.surface: A French meal is served to an ancient Greek author.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the Athenian philosopher who wrote the dialogues.

clue.text: Cat's-paw needs to act with caution

explanation.surface: Someone used as a dupe has to tread carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's paw read literally is a moggy's foot, and to tread warily around an issue is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Doctrine which can make a come-back

indicators.note: making a come-back means the word reads just the same when taken from right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that can return to favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle held as true by a group is a doctrine.
